entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is an externally grounded, socially/legally conferred relation by which a specific obligation attaches to an agent. In BFO terms, this is best captured as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the agent (the bearer), is externally grounded in a normative/legal context, and is realized when the agent performs or is subject to the obligatory act. It is not a Disposition (internally grounded) nor a bare Quality (not merely a measurable property). The 'binding' character reflects the externally imposed, relational, role-like nature of the normative tie between agent and obligation.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023) because it is an externally grounded specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent bearer by virtue of a normative or legal structure imposing an obligation upon them.

AgentObligationBinding is a species of LegalObligation in that it specifically captures the binding relation between an agent and an obligation; LegalObligation already exists as a Role subclass in the working ontology, so AgentObligationBinding refines it to emphasize the binding/attachment dimension.

open_questions: Should 'AgentObligationBinding' be a subclass of the existing 'LegalObligation' class (which is already typed as BFO_0000023 Role), or should it be a sibling class under BFO_0000023 to distinguish legal from non-legal (e.g., moral, contractual) obligation bindings?

Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended as a dyadic relational structure (connecting an agent individual to an obligation individual), or purely as a property/role inhering in the agent? If relational, a reification pattern or an OWL object property may be more appropriate than a class.
Should this class be restricted to legal agents (legal persons, institutions), or does it cover natural persons and moral agents as well?

Is the 'binding' here synonymous with 'imposition' (obligation placed on agent by external authority) or 'commitment' (agent undertakes obligation voluntarily)? This affects whether Role or Disposition is the better BFO parent.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the normative tie by which an obligation adheres to or is imposed upon an agent. In BFO 2020, specifically dependent continuants that are externally grounded and inhere in a bearer are Roles (BFO_0000023). The binding is not an intrinsic, internally grounded capacity (which would be a Disposition), nor a mere measurable property (Quality), but rather a socially/legally conferred role-like relation that makes an agent subject to a given obligation. A new class 'AgentObligationBinding' is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000023 (Role) and refined as a subclass of the existing 'LegalObligation' class to reuse existing ontological structure. Open questions remain about whether the binding is strictly legal, whether it is dyadic/relational in a way requiring a different modeling strategy, and whether voluntary versus imposed obligation should split this into two classes.
